body.x: UniUni (CEO Han Suyeon) has announced its participation in CES 2024, to be held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 9th to 12th.

The company’s name is derived from ‘You And I, UNI’ to signify its services where ‘you and I become one.’ Founded to eliminate various blind spots for vulnerable groups in society through technology, UniUni aims to address social blind spots using AIoT and universal design technologies. With expertise in deep learning, UniUni holds 18 patents, including five registered patents, offering AI-based services.

Having received more than 20 certifications and awards, including pre-startup package selection and outstanding company awards from the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, UniUni is expanding domestically and aiming for global market penetration, recently being selected for the Technology Innovation Program for Startups (TIPS) R&D.

At CES, the spotlight will be on the ‘Savvy Toilet,’ a restroom safety solution. Developed to dominate the global market, Savvy Toilet is an AI-based intelligent integrated solution for ‘safe, secure, satisfactory’ restrooms. It enables 24/7 real-time detection and action based on AI, particularly identifying and analyzing abnormal behavior (illegal filming, falls, unusual behavior, etc.) using deep learning. The solution promises a 99.6% identification rate for risky and strange behavior within 4 seconds, immediately notifying administrators upon detection. The features include real-time data collection, accurate data provision via an automated system, object detection mapping, location information provision through object identification, and real-time monitoring of customer behavior information provided in dashboard format via an app service.

A UniUni spokesperson commented, “We possess a technology that improves the accuracy of abnormal behavior detection (over 98%) by applying optimized AI models for behavior recognition. Our high-precision abnormal behavior detection solution, including non-identifiable IoT sensor-based safety and space management features, is unique in Korea. While competing radar technology exists for detecting illegal filming cameras in restrooms, these focus on post-analysis, making real-time responses based on user behavior analysis challenging. Additionally, regarding disaster or accident response products, similar products are limited to simple storage products for emergency supplies in subway stations or emergency bells that can be pressed during emergencies.”

Continuing to expand domestically, UniUni is engaged in joint business expansion with mobile telecommunication operators like KT and DLIVE. Leveraging these collaborations as references, the company seeks partnerships with overseas mobile telecommunication companies to explore various collaboration methods, such as technological cooperation for network setup, establishing joint sales networks, and devising strategies for business expansion. Since IoT devices require network environments and rapid growth, collaboration with these operators is essential.

body.x: Having participated in CES 2023, UniUni collaborates with overseas mobile telecommunication operators through the GMV program. Collaborations are ongoing with global companies in similar industries like SIERRA HOME HEALTH CARE SERVICE, Legrand Care, Boston University, and JC Deco. Based on these achievements, the company has swiftly confirmed its participation in CES 2024, preparing for global business expansion. Furthermore, it secured seed-stage investment from domestic accelerator CNT Tech and secured investment from Busan through the B-Startup Challenge. It has installed restroom safety solutions in over 30 locations nationwide and has recorded sales of over 100 units this year.

A spokesperson emphasized, “We aggressively aim to secure necessary funds for substantial business expansion through attracting overseas investment. Furthermore, by exhibiting at CES, we aim to showcase our technological capabilities and seek opportunities for our K-AIoT solutions to go viral in the global AIoT market. CES, being held in the United States, the world’s largest consumer market, is the most convenient exhibition for market and customer expansion. Beyond business expansion and investment attraction, we aim to explore and promote possibilities for setting up local offices.”

Continuing, “We aim to dominate the non-identifiable data AI market, overcoming constraints of conventional CCTV-centered approaches. By leveraging behaviors commonly required across various industries, we aim to secure the top position in the non-identifiable data field.”

The Seoul Pavilion at CES 2024, following Seoul’s debut participation in CES in 2020, is operating on its most significant scale, showcasing increased exhibition space, participating companies, and supporters. The collaboration of 13 institutions, the Seoul Pavilion, represents an important step in Seoul’s efforts to establish itself as a startup hub. Among the participating companies, 17 have received innovation awards, attesting to their groundbreaking contributions.

The participating institutions in the Seoul Pavilion include ▲SBA ▲Seoul Biohub ▲Campus Town ▲AI Yangjae Hub ▲Gwanak-gu District ▲Yonsei University ▲Korea University ▲Chung-Ang University ▲Sogang University ▲Kookmin University ▲Hanyang University ▲Konkuk University ▲Kyung Hee University, totaling 13 organizations. The collaboration extends beyond the city and institutions, including industry-academic cooperation in which supporters are matched with companies 1-to-1. Eighty-five supporters, the most significant to date, are participating in this initiative.
